pr.title: Async drop - fix for StorageLive/StorageDead codegen for pinned future
pr.description:
Fixes: rust-lang/rust#140429, Fixes: rust-lang/rust#140531, Fixes: rust-lang/rust#141761, Fixes: rust-lang/rust#141409.

StorageLive/StorageDead codegen is corrected for pinned async drop future.
pr.author: azhogin

analysis.summary: Confirmed bug fix: async-drop lowering for `StateTransform` (`coroutine/drop.rs`) and `Drop` elaboration must emit `StorageDead` for the pinned future temporary on every control-flow path, including the poll-switch block and the unwind/dropline cleanup blocks. Previously the poll switch was built before the pinned temporary's `Place` existed, so no `StorageDead` was emitted there, and `elaborate_drop` only emitted `StorageDead(fut)` in the success block. This left `StorageLive` without a matching `StorageDead`, corrupting MIR storage-liveness invariants and causing ICEs under `-Zlint-mir`/`-Zvalidate-mir`. The `Inline` pass can expose the bad shape (test `live-dead-storage4` runs `-Zmir-enable-passes=+Inline -Zvalidate-mir -Zlint-mir`).
analysis.originalLogic: In `expand_async_drops`, `build_poll_switch` was called before `build_pin_fut`, so the switch block was created without knowledge of the pinned-future local (`fut_pin_place`). The old `build_poll_switch` pushed only `[discr_assign]` into the new basic block. Separately, `elaborate_drop`'s async-drop path added `StorageDead(fut.local)` only at `Location { block: self.succ, statement_index: 0 }`, i.e. only on the success/succ path, while the unwind and dropline paths received no `StorageDead(fut)`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect lowering emitted a `StorageLive` for the pinned future temporary but omitted the corresponding `StorageDead` on the poll-switch path (because the switch was built before `build_pin_fut`, so `fut_pin_place` was unavailable), and omitted `StorageDead(fut)` at the start of the unwind block and the dropline block in elaborated drop. This is not merely a missing cleanup: it violates the invariant that each storage-live region is closed on every path, producing invalid MIR that the MIR linter/validator rejects.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust code using `#![feature(async_drop)]` (edition 2024) where an async function has a value requiring async drop, so that async-drop elaboration builds a pinned future, a poll switch, and (under panic-unwind) cleanup/dropline blocks. Unwinding drop paths and `Inline`-enabled MIR pipelines are especially relevant; no explicit user syntax selects the bad rewrite.
analysis.trigger: Async-drop elaboration of a coroutine/future with a pinned temporary, particularly when the drop path can unwind (panic=unwind creates cleanup blocks) or when the `Inline` pass is enabled, exposes the missing `StorageDead`.
preconditions: A future/value whose drop is elaborated through the async-drop path, creating a pinned future local with `StorageLive`.
MIR validation/linting enabled (`-Zlint-mir` and/or `-Zvalidate-mir`) to detect invalid storage liveness.
For the unwind/dropline variant, panic=unwind cleanup edges must exist; for the Inline variant, `-Zmir-enable-passes=+Inline` must run.
pitfalls: Do not treat the PR as a source-level rewrite; the incorrect transformation is a compiler MIR lowering that leaves storage liveness unclosed.
The fix had to reorder `build_pin_fut` before `build_poll_switch` so the switch block can reference `fut_pin_place`; merely adding a `StorageDead` elsewhere does not cover the switch path.
Unwind and dropline blocks are separate paths: success-path `StorageDead` does not discharge cleanup/dropline liveness obligations.
Panic-abort MIR has no cleanup blocks while panic-unwind does, so a single panic strategy does not exercise the unwind `StorageDead` fix.
`Inline` is a trigger/exposer in this PR, not the pass whose lowering is being corrected; do not attribute the general storage-liveness rule solely to `Inline`.
analysis.testStrategy: Add UI regression tests with `#![feature(async_drop)]`, edition 2024, `-Zlint-mir` and `#![allow(incomplete_features)]`, asserting `check-pass` for minimal async functions (the ex-ICE cases). Add a MIR-opt test with `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY` and `EMIT_MIR ... coroutine_drop_async` to inspect the elaborated MIR under both panic-abort and panic-unwind; verify `StorageDead` appears in the poll-switch block and at the start of unwind/dropline blocks. Include a variant compiled with `-Zmir-enable-passes=+Inline -Zvalidate-mir -Zlint-mir` to exercise the Inline-exposed crash. Update async-drop behavior expectations (the PR changed the expected counter from panic-strategy-dependent `{168}/{136}` to `136`).
evidence: StorageLive/StorageDead codegen is corrected for pinned async drop future.
Fixes: rust-lang/rust#140429, Fixes: rust-lang/rust#140531, Fixes: rust-lang/rust#141761, Fixes: rust-lang/rust#141409.
